### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Selects the $x_2$ and $x_3$ face-flux correction of @sec-ch04-fluxcov: the $x_1$ covariance term
of @eq-ch04-fluxcov-identity and, on a curved grid, the cell-to-face centroid term, @eq-ch04-fluxcov-dF.
**Data.** In: the reconstructed left and right face states of each lateral direction and the grid's $x_1$ face
moments; out: an additive correction to every active $x_2$ or $x_3$ flux, a tracer row for each passive scalar,
and the shifted pressure of the matching geometric source.
**Placement.** In `HydroImpl::forward`, per lateral direction, after the face states are built and before the
Riemann flux is added; the scalar rows in `ScalarImpl::forward` of the same stage.
**Activation.** `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE`, read once per process. **The correction is on by default**: the lookup
falls back to `"1"` when the variable is unset, and `0`, `false`, `off`, `no` or an empty value turn it off
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::flux_covariance >}}). A direction's geometric source is corrected only
when that direction's flux is; the species donor limiter runs whenever the correction is on.
**Guarantee / limits.** A leading $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ smooth-gradient correction that telescopes exactly on a
shared face; no fourth-order claim. Fewer than three $x_1$ cells or a shallow-water state give no correction.
**Evidence.** `test_horizontal_flux_covariance_python`: scaled onset error below `FIXED` = 0.04 with the term
on, the unset arm equal to the `1` arm bit for bit, plain energy drift at most `EPE_TOL` = $10^{-12}$
({{< code tests/test_horizontal_flux_covariance.py FIXED >}}); `test_flux_covariance_rows_python`: rest to
$10^{-9}$, a uniform species to $10^{-13}$, energy-offset invariance to $10^{-10}$
({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_rows.py REST_TOL >}}); `test_flux_covariance_seams_python`: six-panel
totals drift below $10^{-12}$ and the on and off arms differ by more than $10^{-13}$
({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py DRIFT_TOL >}}); check `[C4]` of `configuration_check.py`; the
ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

This section keeps the selector of the lateral covariance correction and the registered arms that exercise it;
the identity behind the correction, the face moments and the telescoping argument are in @sec-ch04-fluxcov and
are not repeated here. The default matters for every reader of a deck: a run that leaves the variable unset
gets the correction, and a run that sets the variable gets what it sets.

### Derivation

See @sec-ch04-fluxcov for the covariance identity, the face centroid term and the exact telescoping of a shared
face flux. The chapter's check line `[C4]` re-derives the linear covariance identity, the mass-weighted mean
and the two-cell cancellation independently [check `src/snapy_report/ch12/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

`HydroImpl::flux_covariance` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::flux_covariance >}}) reads the variable once
and caches the boolean. On each hydro call `HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}})
builds, for each lateral direction with more than one cell and an enabled flux, the correction from the face
states with `_flux_covariance` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::_flux_covariance >}}), adds it to
that direction's flux, keeps the face states for the passive scalars, and lets the geometric source of a
corrected direction use the pressure shifted by the centroid term; a grid whose face centroid shift is
identically zero (Cartesian) keeps the plain source. A passive scalar gets the tracer row of a hydro species
with the same mass fraction through `scalar_flux_covariance`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::scalar_flux_covariance >}}), consumed in `ScalarImpl::forward`
({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}). With the correction on, the species and scalar donor
limiters of @sec-ch08 run even when the EOS limiter is off. No separate MPI synchronization is introduced by this
switch.

: Implementation sites for the flux-covariance selector. {#tbl-ch12-flux-covariance-code}

1. Read the switch once, on unless set to a false token or empty. The anchor `get_env` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::flux_covariance >}}.
2. Per lateral direction, build the correction from the face states and add it to the flux; correct that
   direction's source. The anchor `cov2` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
3. Give each passive scalar its own tracer row from the same face states. The anchor `lateral` is in
   {{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}.

|---|---|---|---|

| `test_flux_covariance_rows_python` (`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0`) | rest, uniform species, energy-offset invariance, `0` and `1` arms | rest $10^{-9}$; fraction $10^{-13}$; offset $10^{-10}$ | `REST_TOL`, `UNIFORM_TOL`, `OFFSET_TOL` |
| `test_flux_covariance_seams_python` | six-panel conservation with cell work and the fixer, direction gating, `0` and `1` arms differ | drift below $10^{-12}$; difference above $10^{-13}$ | `DRIFT_TOL`, `DIFF_TOL` |
| `test_scalar_cov_x1_split_python` (`SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=1`), `test_pref_local_seam_flux_covariance.<b>` (`SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=1`) | the correction on a column split in $x_1$ matches one block | as registered | `tests/CMakeLists.txt` |
| `test_flux_positivity_python`, `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_cov_off_python`, `test_flux_positivity_carry.<b>` (`SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=0`) | the unlimited base arm of the positivity tests, which the default would limit | as in those tests | `tests/CMakeLists.txt` |

: Source assertions, not new solver measurements. {#tbl-ch12-flux-covariance-tests}

The thresholds are `FIXED` and `EPE_TOL` ({{< code tests/test_horizontal_flux_covariance.py FIXED >}},
{{< code tests/test_horizontal_flux_covariance.py EPE_TOL >}}), `REST_TOL`, `UNIFORM_TOL` and `OFFSET_TOL`
({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_rows.py REST_TOL >}}, {{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_rows.py UNIFORM_TOL >}},
{{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_rows.py OFFSET_TOL >}}), and `DRIFT_TOL` and `DIFF_TOL`
({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py DRIFT_TOL >}}, {{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py DIFF_TOL >}});
the arms are set by each script's `main` ({{< code tests/test_horizontal_flux_covariance.py main >}},
{{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_rows.py main >}}, {{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py main >}}) and the
ctest environments by {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}.

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch15-ch12-tests.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
No new order fit is supplied. The centroid term does not vanish for a moving isothermal state on a curved grid;
exact rest needs zero velocity. The correction across MPI-rank seams and XC together with FC have no registered
numerical evidence.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
